At https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Igqr1SOYa88 you can see a fairly substantial non-pressurized habitat. A rigid arm reaches up from its roof about ten metres and attaches to a 3.2-kilometre tether.
 
 It's on Earth, and it hangs from the _side_ of the cable, not the bottom. But it can still illustrate some things.
 
 If the tether were in space, in free fall, and spinning to give the gondola one gee, the gondola could be a "hammer habitat". That means its floor would be cylindrically curved. Its down-hanging distance of 3 km means that its roughly 8-m-by-8-m plan amounts to an angular extent of 0.14 degrees. From its centreline the floor would curve up 0.07 degrees at two of its edges.
 
 But in space, the 3.2-km tether could be lengthened to eight to ten kilometres, reducing the floor curvature to 0.05 degrees. If you asked for a hammer habitat and they gave you one with floors that weren't curved at all, you might not notice. With a good transparent floor, and good sunlight management, you'd be more interested in the underfoot stargazing. The stars would take about a minute to wheel from the floor window's east edge to its west one.
 
 No matter how small the gondola is, it makes little sense to shorten the cable. The optimum distance from gondola roof to spin axis is somewhere in the range 3.577 km (30 rotations per hour for one gee) to 10 km (17.94 rotations per hour). Longer, if cable materials get better in terms of their ratios of working tensile strength to density. Longer and slower-spinning.
 
 Rich people are definitely going to want to own these things, and spend time in them, occasionally dropping in on Earth for short visits. Each will want the whole structure, string, hub, and all, to be their personal property. Slightly less rich people will tolerate condominium or timeshare arrangements. (Everyone will want a bottom-deck apartment because of the above-mentioned view.)
 
 So budgets for their construction will increase over time, and their sizes will increase over time.
 
 The question that should be asked is, at what point does it make sense for this growth to start to be to spinward and antispinward, so that the hammer-headiness becomes more and more noticeable, and suddenly they reach completely around the circle in which the rotation carries them, and you have a Kubrick dumbwheel? No longer dumb?
 
 That would be when everyone who is anyone wants the east and west wings each to be pi times 3.5-to-10 kilometres in extent, and meet each other at their ends.
 
 I doubt this can happen, ever.

Delhi faces several major problems across various sectors.
 
 1. Air Pollution
 
 High levels of PM2.5 and PM10, especially in winter.
 
 Causes: Vehicle emissions, construction dust, industrial pollution, crop burning in neighboring states.
 
 Impact: Respiratory diseases, reduced life expectancy.
 
 
 2. Traffic Congestion
 
 Overcrowded roads due to increasing vehicle population.
 
 Poor public transport connectivity in some areas.
 
 Frequent jams lead to long travel times and higher pollution.
 
 
 3. Water Crisis
 
 Water scarcity due to over-extraction of groundwater.
 
 Unequal distribution: Some areas get surplus water, while others face severe shortages.
 
 Yamuna River pollution makes water treatment difficult.
 
 
 4. Waste Management
 
 Overflowing landfills (Ghazipur, Bhalswa, Okhla).
 
 Lack of proper waste segregation and recycling.
 
 Rising plastic and e-waste problems.
 
 
 5. Crime & Safety
 
 High rates of crimes against women and petty crimes like theft and snatching.
 
 Law enforcement struggles with understaffing and delayed justice.
 
 
 6. Overpopulation & Urbanization
 
 Uncontrolled migration leads to slums and overcrowding.
 
 Basic amenities (housing, electricity, sanitation) struggle to keep up.
 
 
 7. Political & Administrative Issues
 
 Conflict between Delhi Government and Central Government over governance.
 
 Slow decision-making and policy implementation.
 
 
 8. Healthcare Challenges
 
 Overburdened hospitals with shortage of beds and doctors.
 
 Seasonal outbreaks of diseases like dengue and COVID-related concerns.
 
 
 9. Education Gaps
 
 Government schools have improved, but private schools remain unaffordable for many.
 
 Unequal education access in slums and rural outskirts.
 
 
 10. Yamuna River Pollution
 
 High levels of industrial and sewage waste dumped into the river.
 
 Water quality remains poor despite multiple cleanup efforts.

 1. Air Pollution
 
 Solutions:
 
 Strict vehicle emission norms: Encourage electric vehicles, phase out old diesel vehicles.
 
 Public transport improvement: Expand metro, bus fleet, and last-mile connectivity.
 
 Construction regulation: Use dust control measures like water sprinkling and anti-smog guns.
 
 Crop burning alternatives: Provide farmers with eco-friendly disposal methods like bio-decomposers.
 
 Green cover expansion: More urban forests, vertical gardens, and tree plantations.

 2. Traffic Congestion
 
 Solutions:
 
 Carpooling and odd-even schemes: Reduce single-passenger vehicles on roads.
 
 Improved public transport: Better bus frequency, metro expansion, and shared mobility options.
 
 Road infrastructure: More flyovers, underpasses, and smart traffic management systems.
 
 Encourage cycling & walking: Develop dedicated pedestrian and cycling lanes.

 3. Water Crisis
 
 Solutions:
 
 Rainwater harvesting: Mandatory for buildings and societies.
 
 Water recycling: Treat and reuse wastewater for non-drinking purposes.
 
 Yamuna cleanup: Strict pollution control and better sewage treatment.
 
 Leakage control: Fix pipe leaks and upgrade old water distribution systems.
 
 Desalination & alternative sources: Explore new technologies for sustainable water supply.

 Segregation at source: Households must separate wet, dry, and hazardous waste.
 
 Better recycling & composting: Set up more waste processing plants.
 
 Reduce landfill dependency: Convert waste into energy and use decentralized composting.
 
 Strict penalties: Fine individuals and businesses for improper waste disposal.

 More police presence: Increase CCTV surveillance and patrolling in crime-prone areas.
 
 Fast-track courts: Speed up trials for serious crimes, especially those against women.
 
 Self-defense training: Encourage self-defense programs for women and children.
 
 Community policing: Involve citizens in crime prevention through awareness and vigilance groups.

 Solutions:
 
 Better planning of urban expansion: Develop satellite towns and decongest central areas.
 
 Affordable housing schemes: Provide more low-cost housing to prevent slum growth.
 
 Employment opportunities in neighboring states: Reduce migration pressure on Delhi.

 7. Political & Administrative Issues
 
 Solutions:
 
 Clear division of powers: Avoid conflicts between state and central governments.
 
 Citizen engagement: Public participation in governance through digital platforms.
 
 Transparent decision-making: Publish policies and budgets for public scrutiny.

 Solutions:
 
 Expand hospitals & health centers: More government hospitals and primary health centers.
 
 Telemedicine: Improve access to healthcare through digital consultations.
 
 Disease prevention: Regular health awareness campaigns and vaccination drives.
 
 Better emergency response: More ambulances and quicker emergency services.
 
 
 
 ---

 Solutions:
 
 Upgrade government schools: Better infrastructure, teacher training, and digital learning.
 
 Affordable private education: Regulate fees in private schools.
 
 Skill-based education: Introduce vocational training to improve employment opportunities.
 
 Scholarships & financial aid: Help students from low-income families.

 Solutions:
 
 Strict industrial regulation: Fine industries for polluting the river.
 
 Better sewage treatment: Increase wastewater treatment plants.
 
 Ban plastic waste dumping: Enforce heavy penalties for littering in the river.
 
 Community cleanup initiatives: Involve NGOs and local groups in river restoration.
